BiblicalUsage: Shishak was the king of Egypt who gave Jeroboam shelter while Solomon tried to kill him, and who marched on Jerusalem in the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign. He stripped the temple and the palace of their gold, carrying off even the golden shields Solomon had made.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Shishak's march is what a divided kingdom invites. When God's people split, their enemies walk in through the crack, and the gold of Solomon's peace ends up in an Egyptian treasury.
RelatedPeople: Shishak, King of Egypt; King Solomon
